lines.text: When scammers steal $120,000 over instant bank rails, they split it across six mule hops and crypto bridges in under four minutes.
One-hop fraud rules go blind at hop two, while naive single-prompt agents choke on raw logs and freeze 42 innocent nurses' paychecks.
MuleTrace is a speculative branch-and-backtrack reasoning architecture that catches split scam money before finality with zero false freezes.
Through Zetaris federated SQL, parallel Nemotron 30B scouts trace all three outgoing branches across wire, device, and KYC schemas.
At hop two, our Nemotron 120B pruning critic spots Bayview Clinic's verified 42-nurse payroll pool, prunes that branch, and backtracks.
Reallocated scouts chase Branches A and C to hop six, catching $101,500 re-converging at a Kraken bridge with 94 seconds to spare.
Why do linear agents fail deep chases? Dumping raw ledger tables across six hops explodes context past 12,500 tokens and misses the deadline.
MuleTrace runs all four Meterless Engines: Scout Intent scores urgency, and an optimistic-locked World Model tracks tainted dollar conservation.
Meanwhile, Markovian compresses every hop into a compact capsule under 210 tokens, slashing total prompt tokens by 92.7%.
After solving Ring-77 once, MuleTrace commits its headless Nox emulator and 19-second split cadence into H-MEM.
When the same ring strikes a second retiree, H-MEM skips four intermediate hops and locks $79,900 in just two hops and 48 seconds.
And when stolen funds enter a licensed $1.4M title-escrow pool at 64% confidence, MuleTrace abstains from a full freeze and places a surgical $64,000 sub-ledger hold.
Meterless Nightshift powers the entire loop locally, pairing Nemotron 30B for fast hop scouting with Nemotron 120B for pruning and FinCEN freeze orders.
Across five laundering benchmarks and ten conformance tests, MuleTrace recovers $617,800 before finality with zero innocent accounts frozen.
